book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.name: Ascension Primer
book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.toolti: The survival and progression manual for Ascension of Ages.
book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.primer: The first rules of survival and the logic behind the opening era.
The world opens with pressure, not power.

Primitive is about stability. You begin weak, thirsty, exposed, and one mistake away from a limp retreat. Do not sprint toward a ruin just because you can see one. Ask simpler questions first: can you heal, can you carry clean water, and can you survive the coming night or weather shift?

Gather loose materials, secure primitive tools, claim legal wood access, light a fire, and start first aid early. The first quests are not filler. They teach the survival loop the rest of the pack expects you to respect.
A good first day is repeatable, not flashy.

Your core loop is simple: gather flint shards, sticks, and plant fiber; craft crude tools; cut real wood; place a campfire; secure water; and keep a Bandage or Plaster ready. A chest, a fire, and a roof are better than a long corpse-run after dark.

Progress is not the first cool item you find. Progress is a camp that can refill food, water, and healing faster than the world drains them. When you can leave, return, and improve your camp in one trip, the pack starts opening up.
book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.age0_p: Primitive Survival
Hardship, slow food, real exposure, and the first careful exploration.
Primitive Tools
Wood and simple tools are meant to feel earned.
Crude Hands

The early pack setup blocks the normal rush on purpose. Use flint shards, sticks, and plant fiber to get your first primitive cutting tools, then move into wood access, camp infrastructure, and a real shelter. The pack wants your first fire and first safe camp to matter.
Recipe Guidance

Treat the early recipes as a ladder: flint shard plus fiber gets you cutting tools, cutting tools get you wood, wood gets you camp infrastructure, and camp infrastructure gets you survival consistency. If a quest names a primitive tool, craft it before you try to skip ahead.
Water, Weather, and Wounds
LSO makes clean water, climate, and limb damage part of the same problem.
Purify What You Carry

Legendary Survival Overhaul turns water into infrastructure. A Canteen keeps you moving, but a Purified Canteen or Purified Water Bottle is the safe standard. Heat purifies. Smelt or blast filled containers before long trips and carry more than one drink if the route is cold or exposed.
Treat The Right Problem

Food does not solve every wound. Bandages, Plaster, shelter, warmth, and route discipline matter. The Thermometer and Seasonal Calendar exist because the biome and season can be as dangerous as a mob if you ignore them.
Food and Shelter
Early food is slower by design.
Manual Farming Is Intentional

Primitive food should feel manual, local, and survival-focused. Wild crops, simple cooked meals, and a protected kitchen matter more than abundance. Nutritional Balance means one lucky meat stack is not a forever plan, and that is deliberate.
Simple Meal Guidance

Use the quests to push three habits: keep backup road food, cook at least one better meal at home, and start storing ingredients instead of carrying everything. A roof, a fire, and a pantry turn hunger from panic into planning.
Safe Exploration
Exploration is a loop of leaving and returning, not a straight line away from spawn.
Pack Before Distance
Carry torches, a shield when possible, first aid, food, and purified water before you chase structures. A good trip ends back at base with more resources and better information than you started with.
Read Structures
Not every structure is meant to be rushed blind. Learn to scout, retreat, and mark routes. Waystones, compasses, and clue rewards are part of progression, not just convenience items.
book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.age1_f: Primitive Establishment
The first durable tools, the first true dungeon prep, and the first machine footholds that grow out of a stable camp.
Ironbound
Iron is the point where Primitive stops feeling desperate and starts feeling established.
What Iron Means

Primitive establishment begins when the survival loop works well enough to support real equipment. Iron tools, a shield, secure water, and a base worth returning to mean you can start branching into dungeons, treasure, and low-tier industry without pretending you are still in survival triage.
Do Not Skip The Middle

This is still not the factory age. You are meant to become competent, not untouchable. Stronger treasure appears here, but machine-complete shortcuts and next-age power spikes are intentionally held back.
Dungeon Readiness
A real delve kit is a branch milestone, not flavor.
Scout First

A Scout's Pack means a shield, torches, first aid, food, and purified water. The first successful ruin should be a chosen fight with an exit plan, not a reckless full-clear. The quests reward compasses and clues because exploration should become more directed here.
What Unlocks Here

This stage of delving is where the When Dungeons Arise branch and the stronger treasure-hunter branch begin to matter. The reward is not just loot. It is access to better targets, harder locks, and more meaningful routes through the world.
First Works
Your first machine jobs should still feel physical and small.
Recipe Guidance

Primitive tech starts with hand power and simple parts. Craft shafts and cogwheels before you think about scale. Then make a hand crank and a millstone so one real job becomes easier. On the IE side, craft the Engineer's Hammer and one basic component before you treat industry like a solved problem.
A Mill, Not A Factory

The point of this branch is to give you a foothold. One useful machine, one rotation setup, one tool that saves labor. Primitive establishment should teach what machines are for without turning the whole pack into a solved automation puzzle.
book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.treasu: Locked loot is part of progression, not random decoration.
Not every lock means the same danger or reward.

Tier 1 locks are common practice locks. They can fail open, but mistakes still cost loot quality and health. Tier 2 locks are meaningful guarded treasure and do not fail open. Tier 3 is rare elite treasure later in Primitive. Tier 4 exists as future endgame framework and is not part of early balance.

Early Primitive treasure must not skip metal progression. No raw ore, no ore blocks, no meaningful ingot piles, and no easy machine starts. Later Primitive treasure can be stronger, but it still must not hand out bulk metals, complete machines, or next-age power spikes.
Treasure is unlocked through progression, not only luck.

Tier 1 practice treasure is available early. Hard Primitive survival and exploration quests unlock your first Tier 2 opportunities. Later Primitive exploration unlocks the first Tier 3 opportunities. The quests reward maps, clues, compasses, or tokens so treasure hunting becomes intentional.

The pack is trying to make exploration and treasure feel earned instead of passive. A structure clue means something changed in your progression. A tougher lock means the game expects better prep, not just better luck.
book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.food_f: Food starts manual, then opens into relief later.
Diet quality is part of the survival loop.

Nutritional Balance keeps food variety relevant even with LSO in the pack. Farmer's Delight and simple crops solve the early age slowly on purpose. The quests should teach you to keep several ingredients moving instead of one infinite stack of safe food.

Keep one cheap travel food, one better home meal, and at least one crop plan you can sustain. Cook because it improves the loop, not because the quests want random busywork. The slow early kitchen is intentional pack design.
The pack does plan to reduce farming tedium later.

Age 2 is the temporary testing age right now, but it also marks the point where food and farming relief should open up. That is where Create-integrated farming concepts, Create Slice and Dice, and Create Central Kitchen belong as the answer to early manual work.

Primitive is supposed to make food feel scarce, local, and earned. If the first era feels slower than a kitchen automation pack, that is intentional. Later automation exists to reward the player for getting through that pressure, not to erase it immediately.
book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.age2_t: Temporary scaffolding so testers can reach content quickly.

Age 2 currently exists as a broad-access testing age. Its job is to help builders and testers reach systems, bosses, dimensions, and branches quickly while the rest of the progression is still being built out.
Treat Age 2 as scaffolding. Use it to test content breadth, recipe flow, boss readiness, and automation relief. Do not read it as the final balance promise for the pack.
book.kubejs.minecraft_start_guide.future: Frameworks for the later age tree.
The later ages exist as structure now, not finished balance.

Age 3 is planned for deeper industry and longer delves. Age 4 is planned to split advanced magic and advanced industry more clearly. Age 5 moves harder into dimension-spanning play. Age 6 focuses on elite treasure and prestige loops. Age 7 is endgame convergence.
The framework is here early so later editing does not require a full rewrite. Quests, stages, treasure tiers, and guide content are being shaped now to scale toward a much larger progression tree.
